span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A PAPER DISOWNS THE TERM IN ITS OWN TITLE, AND SAYS WHICH TERM IT SHOULD HAVE BEEN: it appears appropriate to indicate that our findings **MIGHT HAVE MORE BEARING ON WHAT MIGHT BE TERMED “COGNITIVE” SETS RATHER THAN ON PERCEPTUAL SETS**. The article is titled “The Role of Frequency in Developing PERCEPTUAL Sets”, and the correction is made in the paper's own voice rather than left to a reader
span.note: about this quote: THIS SPAN CARRIES THE FILE'S OCR DAMAGE, quoted verbatim because a quote is the staged file's bytes. The scan substitutes `th` with `di`/`ti` throughout - `die` for “the”, `diat`/`tibat` for “that”, `tiian` for “than”, `widi` for “with” - so the paper's own sentence reads correctly and this transcription does not. The damage is systematic and was read rather than detected; there is no general detector for it, because `die` is also an English word. See Q-712.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AND THE DISOWNED WORD IS THEN RESERVED FOR A NARROWER CLASS, WITH AN EXAMPLE A READER CAN PICTURE: the term “perceptual” set **MIGHT BETTER BE RESERVED FOR** reference to those instances where a subject **IS LOOKING FOR OR EXPECTING TO SEE A SPECIFIC STIMULUS**, a friend's face in a crowd, for example. Having said the word does not fit their study, they say what it does fit - which is the harder half and the one usually skipped
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE AMBIGUOUS STIMULUS IS DEFINED BY THE TWO CATEGORIES IT CAN FALL INTO, AND THE CATEGORIES ARE NAMED: it **CAN BE PERCEIVED AS BELONGING TO EITHER OF TWO COGNITIVE CATEGORIES OR CLASSES OR OBJECTS: ANIMALS AND HUMANS**. The figure's ambiguity is not a property of the drawing but of which of two named classes a viewer assigns it to
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A GAP IN THE PRIOR LITERATURE IS STATED AS A MISSING QUANTITY RATHER THAN A WRONG RESULT: while Leeper did find that he could control his subjects' responses by manipulating past experiences, he **DID NOT ATTEMPT TO DEMONSTRATE ANY SYSTEMATIC OR QUANTITATIVE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN AMOUNT OF EXPERIENCE AND RESPONSE**. The predecessor is credited with the effect and the paper claims the function relating it to dose
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE INFERENCE FROM THE MEASUREMENT TO THE CONSTRUCT IS STATED AS A PRESUMPTION, IN THAT WORD: **THE PRESUMPTION HERE IS THAT** those with a strong set **WILL RESIST SUCH NEW SET INDUCTION MORE THAN** those with a weak set. What the experiment observes is resistance to a second induction; what it reports is strength of set, and the bridge between them is named a presumption by the authors
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AND THE STRENGTH OF THE SET IS OPERATIONALISED BY BORROWING AN ASSUMPTION FROM A NAMED AUTHORITY: **ASSUMING, WITH ALLPORT,** that having different numbers of such experiences would result in different strengths of set, it was **ALSO DECIDED TO TEST FOR SUCH STRENGTH BY ATTEMPTING TO INDUCE THE ALTERNATE SET**. The premise is attributed rather than argued, and the test for the quantity is chosen after the premise is granted

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE SCOPE OF THE WORD `PERCEPTION` IS LIMITED IN THE SAME BREATH AS THE METHOD IS DESCRIBED: although our experiment makes use of an ambiguous figure, **IT SHOULD BE CLEAR THAT WE ARE NOT SUGGESTING THAT THE STUDY IS DIRECTLY CONCERNED WITH PERCEPTION EXCEPT IN THE LIMITED SENSE OF PERCEPTION OF DIAGRAMMATIC PICTURES**. A disclaimer about what the central word covers, placed before the results rather than in a limitations section

span.label: perceptual set - NARROWED BY THIS PAPER to looking for a SPECIFIC stimulus, with the example the authors chose to make it concrete: a friend's face in a crowd. The paper hands the term back with a smaller extension than its own title uses
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: cognitive set - a set to perceive a CLASS rather than a particular visual stimulus, argued from a case where the stimulus itself was ambiguous: a subject set for a B still reads a distorted figure as a B

span.label: a set that is BROKEN versus one that is REPLACED - the distinction the discussion substitutes for its own procedure's term, available only where a delay was interposed. `replaced` is used nowhere else in the paper, so it is a sense and not a node

span.label: contradicts → Allport (1955), postulate that set strength increases with frequency of past experience
span.note: differs in: THE DISAGREEMENT IS SCOPED TO ONE KIND OF SET, BY THE AUTHORS. 'the present results offer ONLY LITTLE SUPPORT for the frequency proposition that Allport postulates, AT LEAST WITH RESPECT TO SUCH cognitive SETS.' `At least with respect to` is the authors bounding their own contradiction - it holds for cognitive sets and they decline to extend it. (Quote clipped before the paper's own quotation marks around `cognitive`, which are typographically irregular in the staged text - slice, do not retype.) Q-441.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: contradicts → Bruner and Minturn (1955), interpretation of the B/13 result as a perceptual set
span.note: differs in: PERCEPTUAL SET AGAINST COGNITIVE SET. 'EVEN WHEN the subjects are shown a series of letters or numbers with one of these distorted ... as was done by Bruner and Minturn (1955), Quotation withheld; they were COGNITIVELY SET to...' The disagreement with Bruner and Minturn turns on which kind of set the result demonstrates, not on the result. Q-441.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: past experience —causes→ set
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — The paper's opening premise, and the half of it that its data confirm strongly: 75% of subjects follow a single prior picture.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: frequency of experience —causes→ strength of set
span.note: direction on the measure: no-change · strength of the relation: 0.15 — the record marks this weak — THE MEASURED ABSENCE OF THE RELATION THE EXPERIMENT WAS BUILT TO FIND, kept as an edge at weight 0.15 rather than omitted: an omitted edge records that the question was never asked. Pairs with `past experience -> set` at 0.9 - same paper, same procedure, prior exposure decides the response and MORE of it does not strengthen the set. That contrast is the paper's contribution and it is why claim_type is `null-result`.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: one-trial learning —causes→ perceptual sets
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — Offered by the authors as a suggestion - “perhaps in a one-trial learning operation” - and weighted for that hedge rather than against it.
